newsitem.title: JAPAN: Chirac says French policy on Zaire unchanged.
newsitem.headline: Chirac says French policy on Zaire unchanged.

text.p: French President Jacques Chirac said on Tuesday that Paris still believed multinational intervention was needed to help refugees in Zaire, despite the return of many of them to Rwanda.
Chirac told a news conference on the second day of a six-day official visit to Japan that the exodus had caused no change in French policy in the troubled African region.

"France has two objectives...the security of the regions of Goma and Bukavu, and the safety of the airfields and relief convoys," Chirac said when asked if the exodus of Hutu refugees had prompted any change in Paris's position.
"So no, the situation in the area has not changed. It (a multinational force) is necessary for the security of the airfields and food convoys," he said.

"We must provide security and food aid for these refugees and take all the necessary steps to hold a conference under the auspices of the United Nations and the Organisation of African Unity in order to allow the five nations concerned to solve the problem," he added.

Military officials from 14 nations, including France, the United States, Britain and Canada, will meet in Germany on Thursday to debate sending a humanitarian relief force to Zaire, where tens of thousands of refugees are returning to Rwanda.
Representatives to the multinational meeting in Stuttgart will study a detailed report from military assessment teams sent to Zaire and Rwanda.
U.S. officials have said there is no need for foreign troops to provide protection, according to a report in Tuesday's edition of the Washington Post.
But a U.S. State Department spokesman said on Monday that the condition of some 350,000 Rwandans in the so-called Great Lakes region of Zaire was still unknown.
